author: SkinnyguyfitnessCA
body: Omnis pretty good. The Omni spells hit HARD and you'll crush mobs and bosses with them. That said I didn't find them great for raiding because they don't have life siphon.  You'll be raiding a lot as t9. But ymmv

author: Respirra
body: I was necro and changed to bahamut. I am happy overall with the class. All you need to do is buy tamer specialization and CG and you are ready to farm boss gauntlets/world. It struggles with endless dungeons and its raiding potential is average  (I do 1.5-2.2 mln dmg to Apolly in 1 go with Nidhogg). Stack ward gear, buy some supplementary classes like AV or DK and you should be just fine.

author: Tavmania
body:
>I want a class that hits hard, something that makes me go “wow that’s a lot of damage” and +174 magic with Omni is great but I feel it could be better.  

Are you seriously basing this on the +magic bonus that is shown in the Classes selection screen?... Those are base stats after all, and tell you absolutely nothing about the performance of your character in the game in the next tier. As a mage, your equipment plays a huge role in that performance.  

As a Nekromancer that goes into Omnimancer, you WILL be in total control of your BDE damage numbers. You need a T9 god weapon staff (check), and a Dragon's Scroll (check). There are certainly more ways to expand upon those numbers, such as by adding Appolyon's gear (ornate versions give slightly more magic). Heck, I used to equip Cursed Rings against Arthus as an Omnimancer. You also absolutely **need** either Maji or Raider specialization to improve upon your damage, but you can easily reach high damage numbers in both Raids and PVP. (Personal Tip: Heretic's damage numbers are absolutely your style. Only Omnimancer will get you to Heretic at T10)     

If instead, you decide to buy Bahamut next, you are *locked* into exact damage numbers that are nearly independent of your equipment, and are locked into 1 specialization. There is 1 Dragoon's Charm at T5 that slightly improves pet damage, which is great when you have free accessory slots. Here's the plot twist - you generally don't for serious content. Appolyon's ability to Curse+Sleep+debuff you at all times are things that you need to be aware of regularly. Your base HP is low, you tend to gear defensively so that your Pet can do all the heavy lifting.  In the early T9, this will be a blast - Crimson Gazer and Nidhogg will be your best pet. Nobody sees your Bahamut coming, so you are truly blasting through PVP.  

From what I hear from my mates, the life of a Bahamut as a raider is boring. You're waiting for your pet to finish the raid, while you spam ward. However, Bahamut has the large advantage of being able to equip any rarity of Venin and demonforge it for cheap. You don't need a good Venin to do damage, because your pet deals the damage ;)

author: Zafl0
body:
I changed my mind before going Nekro and above to instead go Freyr > Bahamut / Tamer so I can't tell you about mages personally.

Baha/Tamer + CG was a blast with big numbers appearing and clearing Boss Gauntlet floors with 1hits, this to me was your equivalent of ''wow that's a lot of damage''

But! - especially - with CG, you'll live the high risk high reward life on the edge if you don't spam pots. Also the constant dot's and debuffs on you from CG hurt because not only you skip turns due to freeze, paralyze etc. but also take damage and without ward (which ironically is tough to build due to not getting your turn with CG) you also take notable damage over time with burn, rot etc.

If you'd find Nidhogg that would make your life easier but it's not the same big dmg as CG.

There's been numerous times I couldn't even properly buff up and I was at stage 10/21 of a Boss Gauntlet which is cool but at the same time risky if a berserk boss appeared that my CG decided to ignore or not kill in 1 hit. 

In the end I went Titanguard / Tamer with Nidhogg personally for a more safe but still satisfying approach.

Tldr; can't tell you about Omni but Baha is dangerous yet fun and I believe Omni is safer compared so it's up to you which you'd rather go with.

Gl on your decision and no matter the choice, you'll make plenty of Orns until you'll reach 225 so you'll have lots of opportunities to change the class.

author: jonny676
body:
I also took the mage path and ended up with nekro until 200 ish. I then wound up with an ornate ithra blade, so I made the switch to nyx/swash.

It's fun because you don't really have to worry about debuffs, as you want your def to be essentially 0. They also hit like an absolute tank, and as you take damage, the chance you get hit again goes down. Combined with life syphon, you become an unstoppable monster in most situations. 

However, I found the nyx/swash combo to be real squishy at times. Specifically in raids, I was able to hit quite high for Arthus but could barely get my buffs in for Polly. So if you do go this route, you definitely need osmostrike 3.

If you like PvP, dv2 is an absolute necessity as multi hit moves are just terrible in the arena.

I can't comment on other paths because I didn't end up branching out any further before I stopped playing.
